ego.name: Steve Jobs
ego.summary: American entrepreneur, inventor, and executive who co-founded Apple, founded NeXT, and served as chairman and majority shareholder of Pixar. Jobs helped bring personal computers, digital music, smartphones, and tablets to mass markets through the Macintosh, iPod, iPhone, and iPad.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's adoptive father, a machinist who shared his love of mechanics by building with him in the family garage in Mountain View and Los Altos.
connections.notes: Jobs considered Paul fully his father and rejected language that diminished that relationship.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's adoptive mother, a bookkeeper who adopted him with Paul Jobs in 1955 and supported his education.
connections.notes: She and Paul promised to fund his college education as a condition of the adoption.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's biological younger sister, whom he met in New York in 1986 after their mother reconnected them; they became close friends and searched for their father together.
connections.notes: Simpson later delivered Jobs's eulogy and fictionalized aspects of the family story in her writing.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's first girlfriend and an on-and-off partner from their Homestead High School years through the 1970s; they were the parents of Lisa Brennan-Jobs.
connections.notes: Their relationship was personally consequential but often difficult, particularly during the paternity dispute over their daughter.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's eldest child with Chrisann Brennan. After initially denying paternity, Jobs later acknowledged Lisa, legally changed her surname, and reconciled with her.
connections.notes: Their later relationship remained complex and is central to Brennan-Jobs's memoir Small Fry.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs met Powell after a Stanford Business School lecture in 1989. They married in Yosemite in 1991 and remained married until his death.
connections.notes: They had three children together.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's son with Laurene Powell Jobs, born in September 1991.
Jobs's daughter with Laurene Powell Jobs, born in 1995.

Jobs’s longtime friend and Apple co-founder. They sold blue boxes, worked on Atari’s Breakout project, and built Apple around Wozniak’s early computer designs.
connections.notes: Wozniak designed the Apple I and Apple II, while Jobs recognized their commercial potential and led their marketing and product positioning.

connections.relationship_description: Apple's first major investor and an early managerial guide who provided capital, secured credit, and helped incorporate Apple in 1977.
connections.notes: Markkula also became Apple's chairman and played a major role in corporate decisions, including the 1985 dispute that preceded Jobs's departure.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's Reed College friend and early Apple employee. They traveled through India in 1974, later shared a Cupertino house, and Kottke helped assemble and develop early Apple hardware.
connections.notes: Kottke worked on Apple II, Apple III, and Macintosh prototypes and was part of the original Macintosh development team.

connections.relationship_description: Apple’s industrial-design leader who worked closely with Jobs after his return to Apple. Their partnership shaped the iMac, iPod, iPhone, iPad, and MacBook.
connections.notes: Jobs called Ive his spiritual partner at Apple; Ive delivered eulogies at Jobs's employee and family memorial services.

connections.relationship_description: A computer graphics pioneer and Pixar leader who worked with Jobs after the 1986 purchase and spinoff of Lucasfilm's Graphics Group.
connections.notes: Their work joined Jobs's investment and corporate leadership with Pixar's technical and creative development.

connections.relationship_description: Pixar’s creative leader and the director of Toy Story. He worked with Jobs as Pixar became a major computer-animation studio.
connections.notes: Jobs led Pixar as chairman and majority shareholder while Lasseter directed Toy Story, released in 1995.

connections.relationship_description: Apple's chief executive whom Jobs recruited from Pepsi in 1983. Their early partnership broke down in a 1985 struggle over Apple and the Macintosh organization.
connections.notes: Apple's board sided with Sculley, leading to Jobs's loss of managerial authority and resignation from Apple.

connections.relationship_description: Apple operations executive recruited by Jobs in 1998 who became CEO after Jobs resigned because of illness in August 2011.
connections.notes: Cook managed much of Apple's day-to-day operations during Jobs's medical leaves while Jobs retained responsibility for major decisions.

connections.relationship_description: Zen Buddhist teacher to Jobs and Chrisann Brennan who presided over Jobs's 1991 Buddhist wedding to Laurene Powell.
connections.notes: Jobs pursued Zen practice and meditation retreats over many years.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's biological mother, who arranged his adoption and later helped arrange his meeting with his biological sister Mona Simpson in 1986.
connections.notes: She and Jobs reconnected after he sought information about his biological family.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's younger adoptive sister, adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs in 1957 and involved in the family environment where Apple began.
connections.notes: Daniel Kottke described Patricia as among Apple's first part-time board assemblers.

connections.relationship_description: Apple's third original partner, who helped mediate between Jobs and Wozniak, drafted the first partnership agreement, and created early company documentation in 1976.
connections.notes: Wayne withdrew from Apple less than two weeks after its founding because of personal financial exposure.

connections.relationship_description: The Byte Shop proprietor who gave Apple its first major order in 1976. His request for assembled Apple I computers pushed the new partnership into production.
connections.notes: The order forced the new Apple partnership to move from selling boards to producing complete machines.

connections.relationship_description: Atari co-founder who hired Jobs as a computer technician in 1974 and assigned him the Breakout circuit-board project that Jobs completed with Wozniak's help.
connections.notes: Bushnell described Jobs as difficult but valuable.

connections.relationship_description: Reed College calligraphy instructor whose class Jobs audited after leaving the college in 1972.
connections.notes: Jobs later credited the course with influencing the Macintosh's multiple typefaces and proportionally spaced fonts.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs's biological father, whose relationship with Joanne Schieble led to Jobs's birth and adoption in 1955.
connections.notes: Jobs was placed in a closed adoption and did not regard Jandali as a parental figure.

category_summaries.summary: Adoption shaped Jobs’s earliest family life. Paul and Clara Jobs raised him in the Santa Clara Valley, while later contact with Mona Simpson and Joanne Schieble connected him with his biological family. His marriage to Laurene Powell Jobs established the household of his later years, alongside difficult relationships with Chrisann Brennan and Lisa Brennan-Jobs.

Jobs built companies through partnerships that joined product judgment with engineering, finance, design, and filmmaking. Wozniak’s computer designs and Terrell’s first order started Apple. Markkula helped turn it into a corporation. Ive shaped Apple’s later products, while Catmull and Lasseter led Pixar’s technical and creative work.

Jobs’s professional relationships repeatedly changed his role at Apple. Atari gave him early experience in electronics. The conflict with Sculley ended his first Apple tenure and led to NeXT. Cook ran Apple’s operations and succeeded Jobs as chief executive in 2011.

Jobs left Reed College after one semester but continued attending classes that interested him. Robert Palladino’s calligraphy course gave him an early interest in typography that Jobs later connected to the Macintosh.
Jobs began studying Zen Buddhism after his 1974 trip to India. Kōbun Chino Otogawa became his teacher and led his 1991 wedding ceremony with Laurene Powell.
